audit.mode: Read-only bug hunt; source and git left unchanged; temporary tests and fake hosts only.

status_definitions.open: A source defect, requested follow-up, or unverified operational task remains.
status_definitions.fixed-unverified: A corresponding fix is present or reported, but its relevant behavior/deployment has not been verified here.
status_definitions.fixed-verified: The named behavior was checked with a local temporary test; does not certify live deployment.
status_definitions.obsolete: The specific request no longer applies at the audited revision; reason stated.

scope_limits: No real host/lake mutation or production backlog repair.
External Cutok/host/upstream historical facts are conservatively open unless a specific fix is reported; no current network facts are asserted.
Benchmarks in ISSUES.md are historical. The audit only asserts measured local repro results.
Source-policy and requested feature gaps are distinguished from reproduced defects. Passing witness tests assert the current bug symptoms, not desired post-fix behavior.

bugs.title: Eviction deletes the last intact copy; re-ingest cannot repair the corrupt lake object
bugs.observed: See the linked source and witness test, where provided; no production timing or historical state is asserted.
bugs.root_cause: Blobs.held tests only whether any row bears a digest. Ingest trusts that result and skips replacement; evict verifies the tree digest but never the stored payload or chunk completeness.
bugs.abstraction_failure: Presence mistaken for verified custody
bugs.proposed_fix: Make a verified-object contract distinguish present, complete, and intact. Verify lake size/chunks/checksum before eviction; allow ingest to repair damaged objects transactionally. Recheck tree identity immediately before unlink.

bugs.title: Captured evidence aliases different hosts and submission attempts
bugs.observed: Two hosts alpha and beta both have unnamed handle 7. Settle alpha with receipt ALPHA-RUN/alpha-only, then beta whose transcript is empty. Beta settles finished, evidence=verified, and its job.evidence event lists ALPHA-RUN/alpha-only. No network was used.
bugs.root_cause: Captured uses (stream, handle) and default stream is run-<handle>, dropping target and submitted_at. Monitor.capture treats an unavailable/empty transcript as permission to reuse that ambiguous saved log.
bugs.abstraction_failure: Submission identity lost across boundaries
bugs.proposed_fix: Give every submission a durable RunId (target, native handle, submission nonce/time). Key captured logs and receipt associations by RunId, and permit fallback only after an exact identity match. Distinguish unavailable log from valid empty output.

bugs.title: A transient provider log failure is treated as complete evidence and releases the rental
bugs.observed: Fake provider logs('7') raises MissionError('temporary provider log endpoint unavailable'). File pull succeeds. For ordinary train.py, monitor calls cancel('7'), reports ok, evidence=verified, and has no captured transcript.
bugs.root_cause: ProviderJob.transcript collapses unavailable, unsupported, and genuinely empty logs into ''. Verification requires a receipt only for a successful native test with fetch; it cannot know that required log capture failed.
bugs.abstraction_failure: Presence mistaken for verified custody
bugs.proposed_fix: Return a typed capture outcome (captured, valid-empty, unsupported, retryable-error). When supported logs fail to transfer, retain the rental and pending settlement until retry or its explicit release deadline. At the deadline, release with unverified evidence and recorded loss, not verified.

bugs.title: host release kills its running job despite promising to let it finish
bugs.observed: Run a local fake held script that prints ready, sleeps two seconds, then writes a completion marker. Execute Remote.stop as release does. The process exits -15, and the completion marker is absent.
bugs.root_cause: Remote.stop writes cancel/<handle> for every inbox entry before trying its cancelled claim. Claimed submissions remain in inbox, so this tombstones running work even though the claim link fails. Server.execute sees the tombstone and sends SIGTERM.
bugs.abstraction_failure: Scheduler state and cancellation have separate contracts
bugs.proposed_fix: Set stop to prevent new starts, then atomically claim each unclaimed entry as cancelled; tombstone only entries for which that fence won. Preserve already claimed work. Test release while a real local Server executes, not only immediate state parsing.

bugs.title: Automatic pruning deletes source snapshots still referenced by held/PBS jobs
bugs.observed: A nine-day-old snapshot named by an unclaimed held inbox submission is deleted when three newer snapshots exist and no pueue executable is found. The submission remains queued with its cwd now absent.
bugs.root_cause: The only liveness inventory is local pueue; its absence is treated as empty rather than insufficient evidence, omitting PBS jobs and spool inbox/claims. Board.build then also prunes environments based on surviving trees.
bugs.abstraction_failure: Garbage collection lacks complete reachability
bugs.proposed_fix: Build a complete scheduler/spool reference inventory under the same admission/pruning boundary, and fail closed when a relevant source cannot be queried. Preserve the actual running build and every submitted/claimed tree and prefix.

bugs.title: Overlapping needs corrupt the mirror input link
bugs.observed: needs=('data','data/input') rewrote mirror data/input from real-input into a self-symlink, and pin succeeded. Backing input bytes survived.
bugs.root_cause: Live-path strings do not encode ownership or parent-child overlap; _relink follows an already-linked parent into the mirror.
bugs.abstraction_failure: Filesystem spelling mistaken for ownership
bugs.proposed_fix: Canonicalize/collapse live roots and enforce snapshot ancestry before unlinking; skip links already reached through an approved parent.

bugs.title: Center migration omits an externally configured lake
bugs.verification: source inspection; not reproduced end to end
bugs.observed: See the linked source and witness test, where provided; no production timing or historical state is asserted.
bugs.root_cause: Carried.workspace inventories Project.out and snapshots out/lake.sqlite, not Lake.home. Moving the lake outside generated state makes migration omit the durable catalog and blobs while other parcels can report success. This is migration omission, not proof that the original volume was erased.
bugs.abstraction_failure: Storage ownership has no bounded access contract
bugs.proposed_fix: Inventory durable state through Lake's storage contract, snapshot catalog consistently, carry or explicitly retain external data, and verify destination readiness and configured volume before declaring migration successful.

bugs.title: Directory lint can rewrite unchanged sealed inputs and analysis sources
bugs.verification: source inspection; not reproduced end to end
bugs.observed: See the linked source and witness test, where provided; no production timing or historical state is asserted.
bugs.root_cause: Explicit directories expand to all tracked files and writing tools/hygiene run by default; no snapshot/seal registry protects frozen inputs. Exclusions/-text protect known examples but do not enforce immutable ownership generally.
bugs.abstraction_failure: Maintenance ignores immutable artifact ownership
bugs.proposed_fix: Make sealed/registered inputs immutable by contract and lint them read-only. Default broad directory lint to check for unchanged files while applying fixes only to explicitly editable scope.

bugs.title: Lake path containment is lexical and follows symlinks outside the requested boundary
bugs.observed: See the linked source and witness test, where provided; no production timing or historical state is asserted.
bugs.root_cause: within uses abspath rather than resolving filesystem links. Ingest accepts an external file via symlink, and materialize follows a destination parent symlink before replacing the file outside the destination.
bugs.abstraction_failure: Filesystem spelling mistaken for ownership
bugs.proposed_fix: Validate resolved containment for every source and destination parent; use no-follow/directory-handle operations to close check/write races. Reject escaped members before any ingestion or restore.

bugs.title: Materialize replaces an edited file without reporting a conflict
bugs.observed: See the linked source and witness test, where provided; no production timing or historical state is asserted.
bugs.root_cause: Any file whose bytes differ from the indexed digest is overwritten with os.replace, including a newer uncollected result at the same path.
bugs.abstraction_failure: Mutable output paths used as evidence identity
bugs.proposed_fix: Default materialization to missing-or-identical files, report conflicting paths before writing, and expose an explicit restore/overwrite operation for deliberate replacement.

bugs.title: A new reused handle inherits the old attempt's silence and can be declared stalled immediately
bugs.observed: Record old alpha/7 at fake clock 1000. Read a different submitted_at for alpha/7 at clock 4000 with same-length startup output. Its first pulse reports quiet_s=3000 and gpu_pct=0, which satisfies Vigil.stuck's stall test.
bugs.root_cause: Pulse key is target/handle; unchanged byte count preserves the prior attempt's grew timestamp.
bugs.abstraction_failure: Submission identity lost across boundaries
bugs.proposed_fix: Key pulse history by the same RunId as settlement and reset the silence baseline for each new attempt. Use this identity in Vigil's per-job emitted-cell cursor too.

bugs.title: GPU leases do not contend across universes or overlapping device masks
bugs.observed: CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 and 0,1 acquire different files under one root. Two universe roots acquire separate files for CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0. All three acquisitions succeed.
bugs.root_cause: The key is experiment root plus raw mask spelling, rather than physical host/device identity. Separate experiments, mask reorderings, an unset mask, and overlapping masks bypass contention.
bugs.abstraction_failure: Resource ownership is neither global nor atomic
bugs.proposed_fix: Use one host-wide coordinator keyed by canonical physical GPU UUID, acquire all overlapping devices atomically, and have dispatch and trial admission share it. A separate external-process preflight must remain because arbitrary nonparticipating processes cannot honor a file lease.

bugs.title: Held cancellation reports success when its durable fence failed
bugs.observed: A fake login_ask returns exit 4, empty stdout, and read-only filesystem. Held.cancel returns normally.
bugs.root_cause: cancel discards status/stderr and treats every output other than claimed as completion. A failed cd, mkdir, or mktemp can leave no fence and still acknowledge cancellation.
bugs.abstraction_failure: Scheduler state and cancellation have separate contracts
bugs.proposed_fix: Require exit zero and an explicit exited/fenced/claimed protocol response; propagate other statuses as a failed or uncertain cancellation and do not persist a cancelled verdict without durable proof.

bugs.title: Lane submission silently drops execution and data options
bugs.observed: Fake Board.submit received no env, container, fetch, or needs despite explicit CLI options; name/attempt are also omitted.
bugs.root_cause: Single-job and lane paths maintain incompatible partial representations of a dispatch request.
bugs.abstraction_failure: Dispatch branches lose request fields
bugs.proposed_fix: Carry one typed dispatch request into collection and child jobs; derive only target/cell/name differences.

bugs.title: Namespace packages bypass the first-party closure guard
bugs.observed: Armed Guard imported unshipped src/ns/hidden.py; closure.first_party omitted ns.
bugs.root_cause: First-party inventory includes regular packages only, while Python permits namespace packages from editable roots.
bugs.abstraction_failure: Closure proof differs from import and acquisition semantics
bugs.proposed_fix: Inventory namespace portions and validate namespace search locations/child origins against the shipped closure.

bugs.title: PBS acknowledges cancellation even when qdel refuses
bugs.observed: Pbs.cancel invokes qdel with retcode=None and consumes no return status. A refusal cannot change its successful return.
bugs.root_cause: Pbs.cancel bypasses the checked cancellation protocol already used by Line._stop.
bugs.abstraction_failure: Scheduler state and cancellation have separate contracts
bugs.proposed_fix: Route through checked login_ask; distinguish already-finished/unknown from a real refusal and surface refusal or uncertainty instead of reporting cancelled.

bugs.title: PBS command-line select overrides erase GPU requests rendered in the script
bugs.observed: Resources(gpus=2, nodes=1, mem_gb=32) emits command-line select=1:mem=32gb with no ngpus, while JobSpec.directives emits select=1:ngpus=2:mem=32gb. The method itself documents command-line flags as overriding the script.
bugs.root_cause: Two independent resource renderers disagree: JobSpec includes GPUs and the host gpu_in_select policy, while build_qsub_flags reconstructs select using only node count and memory. Interactive requests have no header to compensate at all.
bugs.abstraction_failure: Admission and execution disagree about resources
bugs.proposed_fix: Use one policy-aware PBS resource renderer for script headers and command-line requests, or emit each resource only once. Preserve queue-assigned GPUs on hosts that intentionally set gpu_in_select=false.

bugs.title: Pueue Locked and Stashed tasks are classified as terminal failures
bugs.observed: PueueTask(state=Locked) and PueueTask(state=Stashed), both with no result or exit code, return failed.
bugs.root_cause: The cancellation implementation recognizes these states as waiting, but verdict mapping puts only Running/Queued/Paused in its nonterminal set. Every other state falls into success-or-failure.
bugs.abstraction_failure: Scheduler state and cancellation have separate contracts
bugs.proposed_fix: Map every supported scheduler state through one exhaustive lifecycle table and permit terminal success/failure only for Done with its result. Reuse that mapping for cancellation, listing, settlement and stage text.

bugs.title: Registered acquisition does not enforce a selected frozen source identity
bugs.verification: source inspection; not reproduced end to end
bugs.observed: seal hashes files as they stand on disk, including newly created files. registered checks only that node.md matches those freshly captured bytes. A pre-capture half-edit is accepted; only post-capture edits refuse.
bugs.root_cause: A captured current-tree identity proves which bytes ran but does not prove they match the acquisition's registered/frozen intended source.
bugs.abstraction_failure: Closure proof differs from import and acquisition semantics
bugs.proposed_fix: Add an immutable acquisition source reference resolved before closure creation and compare it with registered source policy; use captured bundle identity without requiring Git as the universal source authority.
bugs.confidence: code inspection; requirement/capability gap, not a claim that present bytes are mislabeled

bugs.title: Relations text preservation stops at top-level keys
bugs.observed: Relations.rows([{'nested': {'date':'2026-10-07'}}]) followed by records returns datetime.date(2026,10,7), and json.dumps raises TypeError. Top-level date/instant/time/UUID receipt tests pass.
bugs.root_cause: The VARCHAR override only marks keys whose immediate value is str. DuckDB still infers temporal types inside nested structures, while records advertises JsonValue but returns raw fetchall values.
bugs.abstraction_failure: JSON and native analytical types share one boundary
bugs.proposed_fix: Define the relation boundary explicitly: recursively preserve JSON strings and normalize records into JsonValue, or expose native values under a distinct typed API and audit JSON serialization callers. Do not silently rewrite historical timestamps without preserving their original representation.

bugs.title: Settling an old reused handle rebuilds and reports the newer submission
bugs.observed: Sweep([old]) rebuilds old.outputs as new.new-output. Scoped settlement of old terminal row sets the newer running row.reported='ok'; old row remains unreported and tracked. The old settlement captures NEW-RUN's receipt. A waiter treats any terminal reported cursor as final even while the newer verdict remains running.
bugs.root_cause: The registry stores full (target, handle, submitted_at), but Sweep calls Board.job(handle,target) and the final report resolves cache.run(handle,target) again; both choose the newest reused handle.
bugs.abstraction_failure: Submission identity lost across boundaries
bugs.proposed_fix: Carry the selected immutable submission through rebuild, capture, transition, and report. Backend calls must prove the scheduler handle still belongs to that attempt; a stale attempt must never operate on a newer job. Report the exact current submission returned by resolve, not another handle lookup.

bugs.title: Two simultaneous GPU sessions can both acquire the same lease; the former owner can delete the newer lease
bugs.observed: Pause acquirer A after O_EXCL creates its file but before fdopen writes. B treats the empty lease as stale, unlinks it and acquires. Resume A: both acquire calls succeed. A.release removes B's lease.
bugs.root_cause: Exclusive creation publishes a partially written record; unreadable records are treated as unowned; stale replacement is check/unlink/create without serialization; the second _write return is ignored and release has no ownership token check.
bugs.abstraction_failure: Resource ownership is neither global nor atomic
bugs.proposed_fix: Centralize acquisition/reclaim/release in an atomic ownership protocol. Publish complete records atomically, serialize stale reclamation, retry losing claimants, and require matching ownership identity on release; distinguish PID reuse with process start identity.

bugs.title: A held settlement lock is invisible while live listing and cached verdict disagree
bugs.observed: A separate FileLock holder makes Monitor.once return running=None with empty failure/down lists. Listing independently probes fake terminal state and renders finished, note='', while cache.verdict remains running. Report contains no owner/start/duration/cache marker.
bugs.root_cause: FileLock is exposed as a bare lock. Contention is reduced to a debug message and nullable running count; CLI/wait do not interpret it. Durable pass has no whole-pass deadline or parent-session lifetime contract.
bugs.abstraction_failure: Public state vocabulary omits freshness and ownership
bugs.proposed_fix: Introduce a lease/claim with owner PID/start/heartbeat and a typed busy result consumed by listing and wait. Bound the pass in a supervised process and stop it when its owning session dies; report fresh scheduler observation separately from stale settlement truth.

bugs.title: Artifact reads and materialization perform one lake query sequence per object
bugs.verification: source inspection; not reproduced end to end
bugs.observed: See the linked source and witness test, where provided; no production timing or historical state is asserted.
bugs.root_cause: materialize calls _write for each row; Blobs.write lists ordinals then queries each chunk. Artifact verification loops digest recalls; query views materialize many receipt files individually. Existing windowed replicate logic is not reused. Historical timings are not re-measured here.
bugs.abstraction_failure: History and files substitute for indexed current state
bugs.proposed_fix: Provide bulk verified read/materialize APIs with bounded windows and chunk streaming for large objects. Query selected run/project indexes before touching files; share reads within a pass.

bugs.title: Dependency rollback leaves new locks and misses filesystem failures
bugs.observed: See the linked source and witness test, where provided; no production timing or historical state is asserted.
bugs.root_cause: _kept records only existing manifest/mb.lock paths and catches only MissionError/KeyboardInterrupt. A failed first install leaves a newly written mb.lock for the reverted manifest; OSError leaves the edited manifest. Generated locks/state and installed prefixes also are outside rollback.
bugs.abstraction_failure: Environment transaction lacks stage and artifact identity
bugs.proposed_fix: Stage edits and all lock artifacts in an operation workspace; publish atomically under one lock only after validation. At minimum restore existence/nonexistence, cover actual failure types, invalidate generated state, and report irreversible installation changes.

bugs.title: Experiment-wide fetch scans every run and rejects rewritten shared output paths
bugs.verification: source inspection; not reproduced end to end
bugs.observed: See the linked source and witness test, where provided; no production timing or historical state is asserted.
bugs.root_cause: Widening fetch repairs sibling evidence stores by collecting an entire experiment home, but every run shares that mutable location. Broad per-pass scans and a fixed transfer deadline remain; conflicting rewrites are not versioned per run.
bugs.abstraction_failure: Mutable output paths used as evidence identity
bugs.proposed_fix: Give each submission immutable output/evidence roots identified by RunId and collect only that manifest with resumable object transfers. Keep a separate shared content store addressed by digest.

bugs.title: Held accepts jobs that can never fit any allocation in the line
bugs.observed: With a two-hour line composed of five-minute allocations, enqueue accepts a six-minute job. Spool.fits rejects the entry even at a fresh allocation's full 300 seconds; renewal cannot ever run it.
bugs.root_cause: Admission checks only remaining line lifetime, whereas execution requires job walltime plus 120-second grace to fit an individual allocation. The actual line capacity is absent from admission.
bugs.abstraction_failure: Admission and execution disagree about resources
bugs.proposed_fix: Admit against min(line deadline remaining, allocation walltime) including grace before publishing. Validate requested memory/nodes/GPUs against the held allocation's recorded envelope as well.

bugs.title: Held allocation lengths at or above 24 hours wrap modulo one day
bugs.observed: _hms(25 * 3600) returns 01:00:00 rather than 25:00:00; 24 hours becomes zero.
bugs.root_cause: Wall-clock formatting via gmtime/strftime is used for a duration.
bugs.abstraction_failure: Admission and execution disagree about resources
bugs.proposed_fix: Render duration components using divmod and preserve total hours; use that duration type in admission, keeper caps, and JobSpec.

bugs.title: Host setup accepts an answering pueued without validating its executable or tool links
bugs.verification: source inspection; not reproduced end to end
bugs.observed: See the linked source and witness test, where provided; no production timing or historical state is asserted.
bugs.root_cause: Successful daemon status short-circuits readiness; dangling PATH links and a daemon running a deleted/old binary are not reconciled. Historical hosts were not queried.
bugs.abstraction_failure: Preparation is not validated readiness
bugs.proposed_fix: Model daemon identity/version/executable and tool-link health in readiness; repair invalid links and plan a safe daemon replacement when its queue is idle.

bugs.title: Host sync retains retired generated files that poison the environment identity
bugs.observed: A retired package-lock.json remains an addressed input beside a current pixi.toml. Generated files are shipped as named members and the target survey only looks up currently named members, so a retired member never enters the deletion delta.
bugs.root_cause: An artifact that represents a complete generated input set is transferred using additive individual-file semantics, while its consumer hashes all nonhidden regular files.
bugs.abstraction_failure: Environment transaction lacks stage and artifact identity
bugs.proposed_fix: Ship generated artifacts as a versioned complete manifest with explicit owned membership; atomically replace/prune only that owned input set while retaining installed environments and host-specific activation/bookkeeping.

bugs.title: PyPI upgrade ignores packages whose actual provider is conda
bugs.verification: source inspection; not reproduced end to end
bugs.observed: See the linked source and witness test, where provided; no production timing or historical state is asserted.
bugs.root_cause: A python requirement gets its floor independently from PyPI, then normal solve retains conda constraints/locked providers; upgrade never requests a targeted conda update. A published PyPI version is not necessarily compatible with the conda-provided distribution.
bugs.abstraction_failure: Published version mistaken for a solvable requirement
bugs.proposed_fix: Resolve dependency identity across ecosystems from the lock; upgrade provider and consumers in one candidate solve, explicitly updating the conda provider when its Python requirement moves.

bugs.title: Settlement repeatedly replays every event in a shared stream
bugs.observed: Four terminal batch runs with 100 existing sample events produce 12 full Journal.replay calls and read 1,240 Event rows. Non-batch track adds another replay. There is no per-pass replay snapshot/cursor index.
bugs.root_cause: Each run reconstructs evidence state once, and each copied/verified event publication reconstructs it again. Cost grows with runs times stream history.
bugs.abstraction_failure: History and files substitute for indexed current state
bugs.proposed_fix: Replay each selected stream once per pass, index latest topic/job/RunId in memory, and update that index as events publish. Longer term persist a queryable projection/current cursor. Profile DuckLake blob file opens separately: Journal.replay selects events, not blobs, so this audit does not assert their exact cause.

bugs.title: Sync still requires a uv-managed interpreter even when the workspace Python is usable
bugs.verification: source inspection; not reproduced end to end
bugs.observed: _sync unconditionally calls Bootstrap.python, which unconditionally runs uv python install. Dialect.python already prefers an existing workspace interpreter. The historical aarch64 download availability was not queried during this audit.
bugs.root_cause: Bootstrap establishment and incremental sync share an unconditional installation step, rather than sharing a required interpreter capability check.
bugs.abstraction_failure: Environment transaction lacks stage and artifact identity
bugs.proposed_fix: Resolve and validate an existing suitable workspace/managed interpreter before installing; install only when neither meets requirements, then let sync reuse the resolved interpreter.

bugs.title: The lake read probe does not bound attach or later volume stalls
bugs.verification: source inspection; not reproduced end to end
bugs.observed: See the linked source and witness test, where provided; no production timing or historical state is asserted.
bugs.root_cause: _answering is cached permanently after one successful read; stat/is_file happen before it, and actual DuckLake ATTACH has no process deadline. The TCC-specific first-read guard cannot bound later or metadata I/O hangs.
bugs.abstraction_failure: Storage ownership has no bounded access contract
bugs.proposed_fix: Put each lake operation that can block on volume I/O behind a cancellable process boundary with a total deadline and structured inaccessible-volume result; avoid opening the lake for unrelated verbs.

bugs.title: Upgrade chooses conda versions available only on the center's platform
bugs.verification: source inspection; not reproduced end to end
bugs.observed: See the linked source and witness test, where provided; no production timing or historical state is asserted.
bugs.root_cause: Conda.latest invokes search with channels but no target platform; the chosen floor is applied to a multi-platform manifest.
bugs.abstraction_failure: Published version mistaken for a solvable requirement
bugs.proposed_fix: Select a release satisfiable on every declared target platform and validate the whole candidate lock before replacing manifest state.

bugs.title: Upgrade selects a yanked PyPI release
bugs.observed: See the linked source and witness test, where provided; no production timing or historical state is asserted.
bugs.root_cause: Python.latest consumes the simple API versions list without inspecting release files, yanked markers, interpreter requirements, or platform artifacts.
bugs.abstraction_failure: Published version mistaken for a solvable requirement
bugs.proposed_fix: Build candidates from usable non-yanked files and validate them against target platforms/interpreters and the complete solve before publishing the manifest.

bugs.title: lock then install leaves second-stage locks stale; existing-prefix run only syncs pixi
bugs.observed: See the linked source and witness test, where provided; no production timing or historical state is asserted.
bugs.root_cause: lock returns before stage resolution. The subsequent install bases resolve solely on whether that invocation moved pixi.lock, so it chooses frozen Node install against changed package.json. Existing-prefix synchronized also never syncs the second stage.
bugs.abstraction_failure: Environment transaction lacks stage and artifact identity
bugs.proposed_fix: Model and persist separate input/lock/install digests per ecosystem. lock resolves every stage; install checks every stage independently of whether pixi.lock moved.

bugs.title: Fresh timeout kills pytest but leaves child workers alive
bugs.observed: Fresh returned124 after4 seconds; spawned worker remained alive. Repro killed it in finally.
bugs.root_cause: Timeout owns one PID while a cell owns a process tree.
bugs.abstraction_failure: Work lifetime is reduced to a PID or exit code
bugs.proposed_fix: Use a shared bounded process runner with whole-tree/group termination and reaping on timeout/interruption.

bugs.title: Lane --wait skips remaining handles after first failure
bugs.observed: Two fake handles submitted, first wait returned1, only first handle waited.
bugs.root_cause: A required wait side effect is embedded in short-circuit exit-code reduction.
bugs.abstraction_failure: Work lifetime is reduced to a PID or exit code
bugs.proposed_fix: Always evaluate every show(wait=True), then combine return codes.

bugs.title: Literal pytest plugin dependencies are not walked transitively
bugs.observed: Plugin shipped, its helper.py omitted, Guard raised ModuleNotFoundError.
bugs.root_cause: Pytest-plugin edges use resolve instead of the common transitive dependency walk.
bugs.abstraction_failure: Closure proof differs from import and acquisition semantics
bugs.proposed_fix: Seed resolved plugin modules into Walker.reach with their owning root.

bugs.title: Malformed runner segments are accepted until pytest runs on the host
bugs.observed: --timeout720 -- -q passed preflight and shipment creation, then collected0 cases and exited4 with file or directory not found: -q.
bugs.root_cause: Runner controls and pytest arguments share an untyped token bag and lose delimiter ownership.
bugs.abstraction_failure: Command structure is lost between parsers
bugs.proposed_fix: Preserve runner and application segments in a parsed invocation; refuse malformed runner-only syntax before shipment while allowing pytest-timeout in the pytest segment.

bugs.title: Pinned-input preflight neither requires restoration nor checks recorded digests
bugs.verification: source inspection; not reproduced end to end
bugs.observed: See the linked source and witness test, where provided; no production timing or historical state is asserted.
bugs.root_cause: _pinned keeps only path and ignores sha256; _restored restores missing paths but ignores the result. EvidenceTree.restore suppresses MissionError and leaves missing objects for the eventual reader. An audit can still run expensive work before finding an absent/corrupt pinned input.
bugs.abstraction_failure: Preparation is not validated readiness
bugs.proposed_fix: Resolve every pin by path and digest before acquisition; verify all hashes and fail collection with a complete missing/conflicting-input list. Keep runtime restore separate from a readiness contract.

bugs.title: Split lanes flatten target and pytest arguments into one target token
bugs.observed: --rerun produced collector token 'test_demo.py::test -- --rerun' and an equivalently quoted malformed job command.
bugs.root_cause: Structured argv is serialized to shell text and reused as a single semantic target.
bugs.abstraction_failure: Command structure is lost between parsers
bugs.proposed_fix: Parse target and pytest argv once and preserve both through collection and each fresh-cell invocation.

bugs.title: --env/--lang/--dev silently omit matching ecosystem or platform dependencies
bugs.observed: See the linked source and witness test, where provided; no production timing or historical state is asserted.
bugs.root_cause: searched builds exact candidate paths and defaults an unspecified ecosystem to conda. Thus --env lab omits lab's Python and platform tables; --lang python also excludes environment/overlay paths unless specifically represented.
bugs.abstraction_failure: Selectors collapse independent dimensions
bugs.proposed_fix: Filter the full declared-slot inventory by independent scope predicates, retaining all unspecified dimensions. Validate --env even when selection yields no requirements.

bugs.title: Calendar versions receive a next-day upper bound
bugs.observed: See the linked source and witness test, where provided; no production timing or historical state is asserted.
bugs.root_cause: Version('20260107') parses as a one-component integer, so generic semver ceiling becomes <20260108 and practically prevents future releases.
bugs.abstraction_failure: Published version mistaken for a solvable requirement
bugs.proposed_fix: Represent version policy by ecosystem/package version scheme; use a floor for calendar versions instead of incrementing the date.

bugs.title: Declared palettes load without the requested perceptual validation
bugs.verification: source inspection; not reproduced end to end
bugs.observed: See the linked source and witness test, where provided; no production timing or historical state is asserted.
bugs.root_cause: PlotStyle validates data shape but does not check contrast, lightness, chroma or distinguishability; no lint step enforces the owner's declared palette policy.
bugs.abstraction_failure: Preparation is not validated readiness
bugs.proposed_fix: Add a style-validation contract with explicit palette checks reused by load and lint, using the existing house validator rather than duplicating rules.

bugs.title: Interactive shell cannot diagnose an already-held PBS slot
bugs.verification: source inspection; not reproduced end to end
bugs.observed: See the linked source and witness test, where provided; no production timing or historical state is asserted.
bugs.root_cause: Board.interact does not inspect the held-line spool before requesting a second interactive allocation.
bugs.abstraction_failure: Admission and execution disagree about resources
bugs.proposed_fix: Consult the shared held-allocation inventory and report owner/expiry and supported reuse path before qsub.

bugs.title: JobSpec documentation still describes the old PBS timeout split
bugs.verification: source inspection; not reproduced end to end
bugs.observed: See the linked source and witness test, where provided; no production timing or historical state is asserted.
bugs.root_cause: The runner now enforces a deadline under PBS, while the public type documentation says queue enforcement replaces it.

failure_classes.name: Submission identity lost across boundaries
failure_classes.invariant: A scheduler handle is reused; only an immutable submission identity may key capture, state, liveness, or evidence.

failure_classes.name: Presence mistaken for verified custody
failure_classes.invariant: Destructive release or eviction requires a complete, intact copy, with failed capture distinct from empty output.

failure_classes.name: Mutable output paths used as evidence identity
failure_classes.invariant: A run owns immutable output roots; restoration and collection must not silently replace another run or a local edit.

failure_classes.name: Filesystem spelling mistaken for ownership
failure_classes.invariant: A path string does not prove resolved containment, especially after a parent is linked to a shared tree.

failure_classes.name: Resource ownership is neither global nor atomic
failure_classes.invariant: One host-wide physical-device authority must atomically acquire, renew and release ownership tokens.

failure_classes.name: Garbage collection lacks complete reachability
failure_classes.invariant: All scheduler queues, spool claims and running source/prefix users must participate in retention.

failure_classes.name: Scheduler state and cancellation have separate contracts
failure_classes.invariant: Terminal state, durable cancellation and graceful draining need one exhaustive transition model.

failure_classes.name: Admission and execution disagree about resources
failure_classes.invariant: Use one resource envelope and serializer for admission, allocation, batch scripts and interactive requests.

failure_classes.name: Command structure is lost between parsers
failure_classes.invariant: Preserve invocation target, runner controls and application argv in a parsed value rather than serializing and guessing boundaries.

failure_classes.name: Dispatch branches lose request fields
failure_classes.invariant: Derive child requests from one complete dispatch request, changing only the fields a lane actually owns.

failure_classes.name: Closure proof differs from import and acquisition semantics
failure_classes.invariant: One dependency graph and source identity policy must cover namespace imports, plugins and a registered frozen acquisition.

failure_classes.name: Work lifetime is reduced to a PID or exit code
failure_classes.invariant: A work unit owns all its children and required waits; failure aggregation cannot suppress cleanup or observation.

failure_classes.name: Environment transaction lacks stage and artifact identity
failure_classes.invariant: Each stage has its own inputs, lock and installation digest, and a complete owned artifact set must publish or roll back together.

failure_classes.name: Published version mistaken for a solvable requirement
failure_classes.invariant: Version policy must account for release scheme, non-yanked artifacts, every platform, provider ecosystem and whole-lock compatibility.

failure_classes.name: Selectors collapse independent dimensions
failure_classes.invariant: Environment, ecosystem, platform and development scope are independent filters over declared requirements.

failure_classes.name: Storage ownership has no bounded access contract
failure_classes.invariant: The lake service must own its configured location, migration, attachment deadline and inaccessible-volume result.

failure_classes.name: History and files substitute for indexed current state
failure_classes.invariant: Batch reads and per-pass projections must replace repeated whole-history replay and file-at-a-time analytical reads.

failure_classes.name: Public state vocabulary omits freshness and ownership
failure_classes.invariant: Listings, waits and SQL need one explicit state vocabulary, including observation freshness and settlement ownership.

failure_classes.name: JSON and native analytical types share one boundary
failure_classes.invariant: JSON values must round-trip recursively; native dates/UUIDs/decimals need a distinct analytical contract.

failure_classes.name: Structured query dependencies inferred from substrings
failure_classes.invariant: Catalog usage must come from parsed relation references rather than textual matches in SQL.

failure_classes.name: Preparation is not validated readiness
failure_classes.invariant: Required input bytes, daemon identity and declared quality policies must be verified before the consuming operation starts.

failure_classes.name: Maintenance ignores immutable artifact ownership
failure_classes.invariant: Tools that can rewrite a path must know whether it belongs to a frozen artifact before writing.
